sections.title: What is ADAS?
body: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) are now standard in modern vehicles and directly impact how repairs are performed. From sensor alignment to windshield calibration, understanding ADAS is essential for restoring safety systems after a collision.

items.title: What does recalibration mean in a repair shop?
body: Recalibration means resetting ADAS sensors after repairs. This is critical after replacing windshields, bumpers, or suspension components, or after any structural work that could affect sensor alignment.

items.title: What is ADAS windshield calibration?
body: When a windshield is replaced, the forward-facing camera mounted behind it must be recalibrated. This ensures systems like lane departure warning and adaptive cruise control function properly.

items.title: What does calibration mean on a car after a collision?
body: Calibration means ensuring all ADAS sensors are properly aligned and communicating with the vehicle’s control systems. It’s a key step in post-repair safety validation.

items.title: Where are ADAS sensors located on a vehicle?
listItems: In the front and rear bumpers (radar and sonar)
items.closingText: Technicians must inspect these areas after any impact.

items.title: Which ADAS features are most affected by collision damage?
items.closingText: These systems rely on precise sensor placement and may require recalibration or replacement.

items.title: What types of ADAS technologies help prevent crashes?
items.closingText: Collision repair shops must ensure these systems are restored to OEM specs.

items.title: What is the expected benefit of ADAS in collision repair?
body: ADAS helps prevent future accidents. Proper calibration after repairs ensures the vehicle’s safety systems are fully functional, protecting both the driver and others on the road.

items.title: What are the six levels of driver assistance technology?
items.listIntro: Technicians should be aware of these SAE levels:
items.closingText: Most collision repair work today involves Level 1–2 systems, which require technician intervention for calibration.

items.title: What does it mean to calibrate a car in a body shop?
body: It means using OEM-approved tools and procedures to realign ADAS sensors after repairs. Calibration is essential for restoring vehicle safety.

items.title: Which alignment procedure may involve self-calibration?
body: Dynamic calibration often involves self-calibration, where the vehicle adjusts its sensors during a test drive under specific conditions.

items.title: What is car calibration after a crash?
body: Car calibration ensures that all safety systems are functioning as intended. It’s a critical final step in the repair process, especially for vehicles with ADAS.

items.title: How do safety devices inside a car help keep customers safe after repairs?
body: Safety devices like airbags, seatbelts, and ADAS systems must be inspected and tested after a collision. Proper repair and calibration ensure they’ll perform correctly in future incidents.

sections.title: Platinum Path
body: ADAS is one of the fastest-growing specialties in collision repair. As vehicles become more complex, shops need experts who can restore advanced safety systems with precision. Whether you're building your career or future-proofing your business, ADAS expertise ensures safer, OEM-compliant repairs and sets you apart in a rapidly evolving industry.
